sources.title: FY2025 issuer results
sources.supports: FY2025 revenue $11.623bn, net income attributable to common shareholders $512m, CFO $2.732bn and non-IFRS FCFA2S $1.683bn

financial_anchor.metric: net income attributable to common shareholders
financial_anchor.caveat: After-tax attributable income governs the hurdle; non-IFRS FCFA2S of $1.683bn is context only.

ai_claim.claim: No consolidated named AI production deployment or measured outcome was identified; vertical copilots remain a research hypothesis.
ai_claim.limitation: Subsidiary deployments may exist but were not consolidated or measured publicly.

strongest_counterevidence.claim: Roper Technologies and generic model vendors and new vertical SaaS products can replicate tools or force gains through to customers.
strongest_counterevidence.limitation: Competitive capability does not by itself prove equal outcomes.

rights_limit: Each vertical product and customer contract differs. Customer records are usually customer-owned; group-wide cross-customer or cross-subsidiary training rights are not disclosed.
materiality_summary: Five percent of FY2025 net income attributable to common shareholders is $25.6m on an annual after-tax basis; no AI-attributed amount is established.

arithmetic.inputs: FY2025 attributable net income $512m; 5%; illustrative eligible labor pool $1.0bn, efficiency 15%, realization 50%, retention 50%, recurring cost $20m; illustrative tax rate 25%
arithmetic.result: Illustrative $13.125m after tax is below the $25.6m annual after-tax hurdle. The 25% tax rate is an explicit research assumption, not company guidance.

g2_provisional: Open: E1/E2 evidence supports measurement, but E3 quality-adjusted causality and E4 cash retention are not established.
unresolved_questions: What share of eligible workload is in production?
What controlled quality-adjusted KPI result exists?
What do contracts permit for pooled learning and how much benefit is retained after recurring cost?
